allowed_claims: Loops can send Supabase Auth emails through Supabase Auth’s Send Email Hook using a Supabase Edge Function and one Loops template per auth email type.

assets.title: Two independent Supabase integrations
assets.content:
Subject: Two independent Supabase integrations
Preview text: Auth email uses the Send Email Hook; onboarding requires separate contact sync.

Separate Auth sending from onboarding sync

Hi there,

Loops is an email sending platform for SaaS teams that supports two Supabase jobs: sending Auth email and bringing synced users into onboarding workflows.

These are independent integrations. Auth email uses Supabase’s Send Email Hook with an Edge Function and one Loops template for each configured auth email type. Sending through Loops also requires a verified Loops sending domain.

Onboarding uses a separate contact-sync integration. It adds Supabase users to a Loops audience, where their contact records can trigger onboarding workflows. The Send Email Hook does not perform this sync.

The Supabase integration guide published by Loops shows both paths and their requirements, so you can compare the architecture with your planned setup before creating an account or changing production infrastructure.

Read the Supabase integration docs → https://loops.so/docs/integrations/supabase

- Loops

value_case.reader_benefit: If the team wants to move Supabase Auth email and connect synced users to onboarding, Loops supports both tasks without requiring the team to treat the Auth Hook as contact sync.

selected_brief.job: Earn an evaluation of whether Loops' documented Supabase architecture fits the team's authentication-email and onboarding requirements.
selected_brief.single_idea: Loops covers the two connected Supabase jobs—sending Auth email and bringing users into onboarding—but does so through distinct, documented integration paths rather than one catch-all connection.
selected_brief.mechanism: Loops integrates with Supabase in two ways: authentication email sending and user synchronization. The Auth Hook handles authentication email; a separate contact-sync setup can add users to a Loops audience and trigger onboarding workflows. A verified Loops sending domain is required.
selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: evaluating Loops may sound like evaluating a single generic Supabase connector. After: the reader sees a specific two-part architecture they can compare with their authentication and onboarding requirements.
must_not_say: Do not claim Loops removes, changes, or bypasses Supabase's own authentication-email rate limit or fixes HTTP 429 errors.
Do not imply the Send Email Hook automatically syncs contacts or starts onboarding workflows.
Do not claim one setup handles both authentication email and onboarding.
Do not claim guaranteed delivery, inbox placement, launch readiness, time savings, or customer results.
Do not imply the recipient has already experienced failed signups, throttling, SMTP errors, or a failed migration.
Do not invent urgency, a deadline, prior contact, or a current evaluation process.
Do not generalize this authentication-email proposition to Clerk teams; Clerk continues sending its own authentication emails.
Do not claim SMTP covers every Supabase Auth email type or conflate SMTP with the Send Email Hook route.
Do not introduce pricing, customer proof, competitors, or the wider integration catalogue.

Keep the connection route attached to its cited source. A native or prebuilt integration and a custom HTTP/webhook endpoint are separate setup paths unless the source explicitly equates them. A platform name alone establishes neither manual endpoint configuration nor a no-setup connector. Keep unknown setup requirements unknown; do not mix the steps or benefits of those paths.
Restrict this campaign to Supabase.
A Loops sending domain must be added and verified before auth email will send (E42).
The SPF, DKIM, MX and DMARC records Loops supplies must be copied into DNS; Loops recommends a sending subdomain such as mail.yourcompany.com (E251, E261).
The Send Email Hook route requires a Supabase Edge Function and one Loops template per auth action type (E1).
The SMTP route requires at least the Confirm signup and Magic Link templates, with Confirm signup's variables also present in Magic Link (E395, E387).
The post-signup onboarding sequence requires the separate Supabase contact-sync setup; the Send Email Hook covers auth email only (E37, E380).

The Clerk branch is only partly served: Loops syncs Clerk users and can run onboarding workflows (E274, E276), but Clerk keeps sending its own authentication emails (E285), so a Clerk team cannot move auth email itself to Loops. On the Supabase branch, SMTP covers five auth types only (E225, E387), an auth type without a Loops template falls back to Supabase's own sender (E230), and unmapped action types are silently skipped in the documented Edge Function (E41). Regional sending, which the audience definition already marks unverified, is not established by the selected evidence, and nothing in the selected evidence speaks to Supabase's own auth-email rate limit.

The documented material names Loops-side prerequisites and failure modes (required templates, verified domain, fallback to Supabase's sender, silently skipped unmapped action types) but establishes nothing about the reported 500 and 535 errors inside Supabase's own SMTP configuration or about recovering after reverting; the report is single-source and undat…
selected_brief.objection: Does supporting both Supabase Auth email and onboarding mean the Auth Hook alone handles both?
selected_brief.next_step_decision: Decide whether Loops' separate authentication-email and contact-sync paths fit the team's planned Supabase setup well enough for a deeper evaluation.
selected_brief.next_step_value: The documentation shows that Loops' Supabase integration covers authentication email and user synchronization as distinct paths, so the reader can assess the required architecture before creating an account or changing production infrastructure.
selected_brief.next_step_limit: Reading the documentation does not establish how Supabase's own authentication-email rate limit behaves with Loops, and it does not verify production delivery or inbox placement.
selected_brief.subject_strategy: Name the specific Supabase handoff from Auth email to onboarding, while signaling that the email explains the two paths rather than promising a generic all-in-one fix.

brief.reader:
Selected audience: A Supabase or Clerk app team moving auth and onboarding email off the platform's built-in defaults before launch.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (grounded; check applicability): Small software teams running Supabase Auth in a real app reach a point — beta registration, App Store submission, opening public signup — where the platform's built-in email sender stops being adequate and auth mail (signup confirmation, recovery, invites, magic links) must be moved onto their own SMTP provider or Send Email hook on a verified domain. Reports in the corpus are concentrated on Supabase; no Clerk evidence appears in the fetched sources.
Qualified campaign scope within that audience: Supabase.
brief.reader_segment: A Supabase or Clerk app team moving auth and onboarding email off the platform's built-in defaults before launch
brief.promise: A Supabase team can use Loops for both authentication email and post-signup onboarding through two documented integration paths, while evaluating the requirements of each separately.
brief.orientation: Loops is an email sending platform that can send Supabase Auth email and, through separate contact sync, trigger onboarding workflows for synced users.
brief.arc: Introduce the two-part Supabase use case, make the separation and verified-domain requirement explicit, then direct the reader to the documentation to decide whether the architecture fits.
brief.sequence_rationale: There is one email, so it must stand alone. It leads with the mechanism most closely matched to the reader's job, answers the likely scope question that the Auth Hook does not itself sync contacts, and uses a read-only documentation page as the lowest-friction next step for an unknown relationship. No alternative proposition is included because pricing or a narrower SMTP argument would be less directly tied to evaluating the full auth-and-onboarding job.

emails.selection_reason: The selected Supabase team needs to assess both authentication sending and the handoff into onboarding. The documented two-path integration makes that fit question concrete without promising that Loops changes Supabase's own rate limits.

value_case.reader_benefit: If the team wants to move Supabase Auth email and connect synced users to onboarding, Loops supports both tasks without requiring the team to treat the Auth Hook as contact sync.
value_case.mechanism: Loops documents two Supabase integration paths: authentication email sending and user synchronization. The Send Email Hook covers authentication email only; the separate contact-sync integration can add users to a Loops audience and trigger workflows. Sending through Loops requires a verified Loops sending domain.
decision_conditions: This proposition applies to Supabase, not the broader Clerk branch.
Authentication email and contact-triggered onboarding require separate integration paths.
A verified Loops sending domain is required for sending.

emails.target_audience: A Supabase or Clerk app team moving auth and onboarding email off the platform's built-in defaults before launch
emails.job: Earn an evaluation of whether Loops' documented Supabase architecture fits the team's authentication-email and onboarding requirements.
emails.single_idea: Loops covers the two connected Supabase jobs—sending Auth email and bringing users into onboarding—but does so through distinct, documented integration paths rather than one catch-all connection.
emails.mechanism: Loops integrates with Supabase in two ways: authentication email sending and user synchronization. The Auth Hook handles authentication email; a separate contact-sync setup can add users to a Loops audience and trigger onboarding workflows. A verified Loops sending domain is required.
emails.belief_shift: Before: evaluating Loops may sound like evaluating a single generic Supabase connector. After: the reader sees a specific two-part architecture they can compare with their authentication and onboarding requirements.
must_not_say: Do not claim Loops removes, changes, or bypasses Supabase's own authentication-email rate limit or fixes HTTP 429 errors.
Do not imply the Send Email Hook automatically syncs contacts or starts onboarding workflows.
Do not claim one setup handles both authentication email and onboarding.
Do not claim guaranteed delivery, inbox placement, launch readiness, time savings, or customer results.
Do not imply the recipient has already experienced failed signups, throttling, SMTP errors, or a failed migration.
Do not invent urgency, a deadline, prior contact, or a current evaluation process.
Do not generalize this authentication-email proposition to Clerk teams; Clerk continues sending its own authentication emails.
Do not claim SMTP covers every Supabase Auth email type or conflate SMTP with the Send Email Hook route.
Do not introduce pricing, customer proof, competitors, or the wider integration catalogue.

Keep the connection route attached to its cited source. A native or prebuilt integration and a custom HTTP/webhook endpoint are separate setup paths unless the source explicitly equates them. A platform name alone establishes neither manual endpoint configuration nor a no-setup connector. Keep unknown setup requirements unknown; do not mix the steps or benefits of those paths.
Restrict this campaign to Supabase.
A Loops sending domain must be added and verified before auth email will send (E42).
The SPF, DKIM, MX and DMARC records Loops supplies must be copied into DNS; Loops recommends a sending subdomain such as mail.yourcompany.com (E251, E261).
The Send Email Hook route requires a Supabase Edge Function and one Loops template per auth action type (E1).
The SMTP route requires at least the Confirm signup and Magic Link templates, with Confirm signup's variables also present in Magic Link (E395, E387).
The post-signup onboarding sequence requires the separate Supabase contact-sync setup; the Send Email Hook covers auth email only (E37, E380).

The Clerk branch is only partly served: Loops syncs Clerk users and can run onboarding workflows (E274, E276), but Clerk keeps sending its own authentication emails (E285), so a Clerk team cannot move auth email itself to Loops. On the Supabase branch, SMTP covers five auth types only (E225, E387), an auth type without a Loops template falls back to Supabase's own sender (E230), and unmapped action types are silently skipped in the documented Edge Function (E41). Regional sending, which the audience definition already marks unverified, is not established by the selected evidence, and nothing in the selected evidence speaks to Supabase's own auth-email rate limit.

The documented material names Loops-side prerequisites and failure modes (required templates, verified domain, fallback to Supabase's sender, silently skipped unmapped action types) but establishes nothing about the reported 500 and 535 errors inside Supabase's own SMTP configuration or about recovering after reverting; the report is single-source and undat…
emails.objection: Does supporting both Supabase Auth email and onboarding mean the Auth Hook alone handles both?
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Loops' separate authentication-email and contact-sync paths fit the team's planned Supabase setup well enough for a deeper evaluation.
emails.next_step_value: The documentation shows that Loops' Supabase integration covers authentication email and user synchronization as distinct paths, so the reader can assess the required architecture before creating an account or changing production infrastructure.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading the documentation does not establish how Supabase's own authentication-email rate limit behaves with Loops, and it does not verify production delivery or inbox placement.
emails.subject_strategy: Name the specific Supabase handoff from Auth email to onboarding, while signaling that the email explains the two paths rather than promising a generic all-in-one fix.

brief.voice_notes: Use Loops' short, declarative style. Keep technical terms concrete. Avoid hype, unsupported ease claims, and language that assumes the reader is currently blocked.

reasons: Verified product evidence covers only the stated alternative: Supabase.
allowed_claims: Loops can send Supabase Auth emails through Supabase Auth’s Send Email Hook using a Supabase Edge Function and one Loops template per auth email type.
Supabase Auth’s Send Email Hook can send emails through a controlled HTTP endpoint instead of Supabase’s sender.
The documented Supabase Edge Function verifies Send Email Hook requests and sends the corresponding Loops transactional email.
The Edge Function can verify the Supabase request signature, map email_action_type to a Loops transactional email, and send it through the Loops API with Supabase-provided tokens and links.
Loops templates are only required for the Supabase auth action types a team uses; an action type without a matching template falls back to Supabase’s default sender.
Loops supports a Confirm signup template for Supabase’s signup action type with token, tokenHash, redirectTo, and siteUrl variables.
Loops supports an Invite user template for Supabase’s invite action type with token, tokenHash, redirectTo, and siteUrl variables.
Loops supports a Magic link template for Supabase’s magiclink action type with token, tokenHash, redirectTo, and siteUrl variables.
Loops supports a Reset password template for Supabase’s recovery action type with token, tokenHash, redirectTo, and siteUrl variables.
Loops supports a Change email address template for Supabase’s email_change action type with token, tokenHash, tokenNew, tokenHashNew, redirectTo, and siteUrl variables.
Loops supports a Reauthentication template for Supabase’s reauthentication action type with token and tokenHash variables.
Loops supports a password-changed security-notification template for Supabase’s password_changed_notification action type.
Loops supports an email-changed security-notification template for Supabase’s email_changed_notification action type with an oldEmail variable.
Loops supports a phone-changed security-notification template for Supabase’s phone_changed_notification action type with an oldPhone variable.
Loops supports an identity-linked security-notification template for Supabase’s identity_linked_notification action type with a provider variable.
Loops supports an identity-unlinked security-notification template for Supabase’s identity_unlinked_notification action type with a provider variable.
Loops supports an MFA-factor-enrolled security-notification template for Supabase’s mfa_factor_enrolled_notification action type with a factorType variable.
Loops supports an MFA-factor-unenrolled security-notification template for Supabase’s mfa_factor_unenrolled_notification action type with a factorType variable.
A Loops token data variable can display a 6-digit OTP code.
A clickable authentication URL can be built from the siteUrl, tokenHash, and redirectTo data variables.
The documented Edge Function maps email_action_type values to Loops transactional IDs and sends emails with the Loops SDK.
Loops ignores sent data-variable values that do not match a variable on the transactional template.
Loops transactional sends can be checked on the Loops Transactional page.
A 401 in Supabase Auth logs usually indicates that SEND_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET does not match the Hooks-page secret.
Loops authentication templates can be updated programmatically with the Update an email message API.
The Loops Update an email message API accepts expectedRevisionId and returns 409 Conflict when the revision has changed since it was fetched.
Loops email-message APIs can be used to keep subject lines, preview text, or LMX content in version control and deploy changes through a script or CI job.
The Send Email Hook approach covers all Send Email Hook action types, including security notifications; Loops SMTP covers confirm signup, magic link, invite, change email, and reset password.
Loops Send Email Hook and Loops SMTP use the same Loops transactional emails, allowing a move from SMTP to the hook without rebuilding templates.
The Send Email Hook covers auth emails only; the Supabase contact-sync integration can sync users into a Loops audience and trigger workflows.
A Supabase database webhook can create or update Loops contacts on INSERT and UPDATE events for auth.users.
A Loops workflow can be triggered by an auth.users INSERT event to send a welcome or onboarding sequence after signup.
A Loops transactional email must be published for it to send in this integration.
Unmapped Supabase email_action_type values are silently skipped rather than producing an error in the documented implementation.
Sending through Loops requires a verified Loops sending domain.

intelligence.selected_audience: A Supabase or Clerk app team moving auth and onboarding email off the platform's built-in defaults before launch
partial_caveats_injected: A Loops sending domain must be added and verified before auth email will send (E42).
The SPF, DKIM, MX and DMARC records Loops supplies must be copied into DNS; Loops recommends a sending subdomain such as mail.yourcompany.com (E251, E261).
The Send Email Hook route requires a Supabase Edge Function and one Loops template per auth action type (E1).
The SMTP route requires at least the Confirm signup and Magic Link templates, with Confirm signup's variables also present in Magic Link (E395, E387).
The post-signup onboarding sequence requires the separate Supabase contact-sync setup; the Send Email Hook covers auth email only (E37, E380).

The Clerk branch is only partly served: Loops syncs Clerk users and can run onboarding workflows (E274, E276), but Clerk keeps sending its own authentication emails (E285), so a Clerk team cannot move auth email itself to Loops. On the Supabase branch, SMTP covers five auth types only (E225, E387), an auth type without a Loops template falls back to Supabase's own sender (E230), and unmapped action types are silently skipped in the documented Edge Function (E41). Regional sending, which the audience definition already marks unverified, is not established by the selected evidence, and nothing in the selected evidence speaks to Supabase's own auth-email rate limit.

The documented material names Loops-side prerequisites and failure modes (required templates, verified domain, fallback to Supabase's sender, silently skipped unmapped action types) but establishes nothing about the reported 500 and 535 errors inside Supabase's own SMTP configuration or about recovering after reverting; the report is single-source and undat…
